---
title: "Public schema privatization"
description: "Staged plan that moves every application table, view and RPC out of the PostgREST-exposed public schema into the service-only private schema."
updatedAt: '2026-11-17'
audience: developers
---

The `public` schema is reachable by every browser, mobile client and holder of
the anon key through PostgREST. Row Level Security is the fence for every
table that still grants client roles, so one missing or permissive policy
exposes a table. `20260522172925_harden_proxy_only_public_tables.sql` revoked
the `public` default privileges on tables, sequences and functions for
`current_user`, `postgres` and the `supabase_*` owner roles the migration role
belongs to. `20261027151200_restrict_anon_definer_execute.sql` can re-grant
default function EXECUTE to `authenticated` or `service_role` where that access
came from the implicit global `PUBLIC` default. Platform-owned default ACLs
(owner `supabase_admin`) still grant client roles in a full local replay; those
apply only to objects that role creates.

The target is a `public` schema with no application relations. Application data
lives in `private`, which `anon` and `authenticated` cannot use, and clients
reach it only through server routes that authorize the actor first.

This page is the plan. It applies no migration and is not production
authorization: every production database change in it needs its own approval
(see [Approvals](#approvals-and-review)).

## Current state

Inventory from checked-in source on 2026-11-17 (generated types in
`packages/types/src/supabase.ts`, migrations in
`apps/database/supabase/migrations`). Generated types are a source snapshot;
confirm hosted catalog state on a disposable replay before each wave.

| Schema | Tables | Views | Functions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | 293 | 27 | 454 |
| `private` | 390 | 14 | 547 |

The move is an established pattern: 65 migrations named `*private*` (for
example `20260521155712_move_more_tables_private.sql` and
`20260528141100_move_inventory_tables_private.sql`) moved tables with
`ALTER TABLE … SET SCHEMA private`, revoked client roles, added a
`service_role` policy and re-pinned dependent function `search_path`s.
`private` is listed in `[api].schemas` (`apps/database/supabase/config.toml`)
so the server can call `.schema('private')`, while `USAGE` is revoked from
`public`, `anon` and `authenticated`. 569 source files already use
`.schema('private')`.

### Direct callers

Lexical scan of `.from('<table>')` and `.rpc('<fn>')` in `apps/*` and
`packages/*` (TypeScript, excluding tests, `backend`, `tanstack-web`), Dart in
`apps/mobile/lib`, and Python in `apps/discord`. A file is classified as:

- **browser**: a `'use client'` module or one that imports the browser
  Supabase client;
- **rls**: a server module without an admin client, so the query runs as the
  user and depends on RLS;
- **admin**: a server module that creates a service-role client.

| Surface | Direct public access today | Migration impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web and satellite browser modules | 35 tables in modules of 15 apps/packages, 9 RPCs (`generate_cross_app_token`, `has_workspace_permission`, `get_user_workspace_subscription_info`, three `get_finance_invoice_*_by_workspace`, cross-app token validate/revoke, `get_user_whitelist_status`) | Replace with `@tuturuuu/internal-api` calls to owning routes. The [browser session-surface guard](/build/development-tools/browser-session-surface) already blocks new browser clients. |
| Server modules on the user client (rls) | 199 tables across 31 apps/packages; heaviest in `apps/web`, `apps/tasks`, `apps/infrastructure`, `apps/finance`, `apps/teach` | Authorize with the request client, then read/write through the admin client on `private`, following the workspace-scoped write rules in the database skill. Satellites resolve actors with `getSatelliteAppSessionUser`. |
| Server modules on the admin client | 217 tables across 40 apps/packages | Mechanical: `.from(x)` becomes `.schema('private').from(x)`. |
| Mobile (Flutter `supabase_flutter`) | `user_private_details`, `workspace_members`, `workspaces`, `wallet_transactions`, `workspace_role_members`, `workspace_default_permissions` (11 call sites in 4 files); no RPCs, no `postgres_changes` | New `/api/v1` endpoints, a store release, and a minimum-version gate before revocation. |
| Discord bot (Python, service role) | `workspace_boards`, `task_lists`, `tasks`, `task_assignees`, `discord_integrations`, `discord_guild_members`, `workspace_members`, `shortened_links`, `time_tracking_sessions`, `meet_together_plans` | Switch to `supabase.schema("private").table(...)` per wave; no client exposure. |
| SDK and CLI (`packages/sdk`) | None; all calls go through `@tuturuuu/internal-api` | API contract stability only. |
| Realtime | 0 `postgres_changes` subscriptions in TS and Dart; broadcast channels use server-issued tickets (`apps/web/src/app/api/v1/realtime/channels/route.ts`) and the Cloudflare `chat-realtime`, `hive-realtime`, `meet-realtime` Durable Objects | Drop moved tables from the `supabase_realtime` publication (notifications, task labels, legacy chat tables are still members). |
| Workers and Edge Functions | No Worker touches `public` tables directly; there are no Supabase Edge Functions | None. |
| Storage policies | `workspaces` bucket policies call `workspace_storage.*` helpers that read membership and role tables | Helpers must keep working for `authenticated` after Wave 8 (see [RLS helpers](#rls-helpers-and-storage-policies)). |

The per-table classification is in the [appendix](#appendix-table-inventory).
`no-ts-caller` means no lexical TypeScript, Dart or Python caller; such tables
can still be read by SQL functions, triggers or views, so check `pg_depend` and
function bodies before treating them as dead.

### Sensitivity classes

1. **Secrets, credentials and auth state**: encrypted secrets, OAuth tokens,
   API keys, mail credentials, payment provider connections, QR login,
   abuse/suspension controls, platform roles.
2. **Billing and money**: subscriptions, credit balances, invoices, wallets,
   transactions, payroll/compensation.
3. **Mail and PII**: sent mail, audit, blacklists, notifications and push
   devices, inquiries and feedback, user and workspace-user profiles.
4. **Workspace content**: AI chats, meeting AI, Mira, tasks, time tracking,
   calendars, courses, quizzes, external projects.
5. **Public catalogs**: changelog, holidays, exchange rates, short links,
   public polls and Meet Together plans.

## Target pattern

### Data access

- **Tables and views** live in `private`, `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, with one
  `FOR ALL TO service_role` policy and `REVOKE ALL … FROM public, anon,
  authenticated`. Views are `security_invoker`.
- **Server routes own access.** Each route resolves the actor, checks
  workspace membership and permission with the request-scoped client, then uses
  the admin client on `private` and keeps every child read and write scoped to
  the verified workspace. Shared data access stays in `packages/internal-api`
  and the domain `*-core` packages; framework adapters inject the client.
  New handlers go under `apps/web/src/app/api/**`, not `legacy-api-routes/**`.
- **RPCs.** A function that touches only private tables moves to `private`,
  executable by `service_role` only. Functions that rely on `auth.uid()` take an
  explicit `p_actor_id` the server resolves, and keep their internal workspace
  checks. A `public` function survives only on the guard's function allowlist
  (see [Guard](#guard-no-new-public-relations)) with an `auth.uid()` check,
  pinned `search_path` ending in `pg_temp`, and explicit grants.
- **Rollout fallback.** Production migrations apply after the production
  deployment marker, so code ships before the move. Each moved table is read
  through a helper that targets `private` first and falls back to `public` on
  `42P01`, `PGRST106` or `PGRST205`, caching the resolved schema per process
  (precedent: `packages/education-core/src/education/private-quiz-answers.ts`).
  The fallback is removed in the next wave once the move is confirmed in
  production. Rollback of a move therefore needs no code deploy.

### Compatibility views

Do not create client-granted compatibility views in `public`. A
`security_invoker` view fails once the client loses `private` access, and a
definer view re-creates the exposure. The only allowed form is a
`service_role`-only `public.<name>` view over `private.<name>` when a
service-role caller (for example the Discord bot) cannot ship in time, recorded
on the allowlist with an expiry wave. Mobile compatibility comes from the
release window, not from views.

### Realtime

Clients keep subscribing to private Broadcast channels with the server-issued
join ticket. Mutating routes publish after commit (server fan-out through
Realtime broadcast or the owning Durable Object). Moving a table never adds a
`postgres_changes` subscription; the browser session-surface guard keeps that
count at 0. Each wave removes its moved tables from the `supabase_realtime`
publication after confirming no subscriber in the realtime log aggregation.

### Mobile and SDK

- Each mobile table gets a versioned `/api/v1/...` endpoint and a
  `check-mobile-api-mappings` entry. The app switches in one release (Mobile
  release M1) shipped before Wave 2.
- Revocation of a mobile table waits until the `version-check` minimum
  supported version is at or above M1 and the old-version share of authenticated
  traffic is below the agreed threshold (default: under 2% for 14 days).
- The SDK is unaffected at the data layer. Any route whose response shape
  changes keeps the old shape for one minor SDK release.

### RLS helpers and storage policies

Policies run as the querying role. Once a table is private, any `public`
policy, view or invoker function that reads it fails for `authenticated`. Per
wave:

1. On a disposable full replay, list dependents with `pg_depend` and scan
   `pg_proc.prosrc` for the table name (PL/pgSQL bodies are not tracked by
   `pg_depend`).
2. Re-pin dependent function `search_path` to `public, private, pg_temp` or
   qualify references.
3. Membership and permission helpers that client-facing policies still need
   (storage `workspaces` bucket, any remaining client RLS) move to a
   non-exposed helper schema, following `workspace_storage`: not in
   `[api].schemas`, `USAGE` granted to `authenticated`, functions
   `SECURITY DEFINER` with pinned path and EXECUTE only for the roles their
   policies run as.
4. Re-run `security-definer-search-paths.sql`,
   `security-definer-policy-callers.sql` and
   `workspace-storage-least-privilege-rls.sql`.

### Generated types

`bun sb:typegen` already emits `public,private,storage`. After each local apply,
regenerate and commit; shared row aliases in `packages/types/src/db.ts` point at
`Database['private']['Tables'][…]`. Never hand-edit generated files.

## Wave mechanics

Every wave runs the same three phases. Each phase is a separate commit set.

| Phase | Change | Production DB change | Rollback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Server-first code | Callers move to server routes / admin client with the private-first fallback; mobile endpoints added | None | Revert commit |
| B. Revoke | `REVOKE ALL ON public.<t> FROM anon, authenticated`; drop client policies; remove from `supabase_realtime` | Yes (approval) | Prepared `rollbacks/` migration re-grants the captured ACLs and recreates the captured policies |
| C. Move | `ALTER TABLE public.<t> SET SCHEMA private`; service-role policy; dependent `search_path` fixes; move wave RPCs; `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'`; typegen | Yes (approval) | `SET SCHEMA public` and recreate prior function definitions from the full-chain catalog; fallback keeps code working |

Phase B of wave N+1 and phase C of wave N can share one migration batch and one
approval. Migration rules:

- `SET SCHEMA` takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock briefly: set `lock_timeout`
  (for example `'3s'`) and keep each table move short. Keep DDL, constraint
  validation and concurrent index work in separate files.
- Capture ACLs including grantors and grant options, policy definitions and
  function definitions before the change so the rollback restores exactly.
  Never re-grant `PUBLIC` or `anon` in a rollback that did not have them.
- Migrations that touch pg_cron targets execute the stored `cron.job.command`
  on the disposable chain.
- Apply locally (`bun sb:reset`) through `ttr resources run`, then typegen.
  Production runs only through `supabase-production.yaml` after the staging
  marker; never `bun sb:push`.

### Tests per wave

- **pgTAP `private-schema-client-denial.sql`** (new, extended each wave): for
  every relation in `private`, `has_table_privilege` is false for `anon` and
  `authenticated` on SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; `has_schema_privilege`
  on `private` USAGE is false for both; every function in `private` is not
  executable by `PUBLIC`, `anon` or `authenticated`; each wave's tables exist in
  `private` and not in `public`.
- **HTTP denial check** against local PostgREST: anon key and a user JWT get
  `PGRST205`/404 for `/rest/v1/<t>` and a permission error with
  `Accept-Profile: private`.
- **Source "no direct client access" check** (part of the guard): no moved
  table appears in a browser module, a Dart `.from(...)`, a Python
  `.table(...)` without `schema("private")`, or a TypeScript `.from(...)`
  without a preceding `.schema('private')` or the fallback helper.
- Focused route tests for every changed route (authorization 401/403/500
  mapping, workspace scoping, actor stamping) and the existing domain pgTAP
  suites for moved RPCs.
- Mobile: repository tests against the new endpoints; `flutter gen-l10n` only
  if strings change.
- Exact-commit CI: Web build and each touched satellite build, type-check,
  lint, test. No local builds.

## Waves

ETAs are focused agent-days for implementation, review and verification,
excluding store review and approval waits. Waves 5, 6 and 7 are independent and
can run in parallel lanes after Wave 4.

| Wave | Scope | Relations | Notable callers | Mobile | ETA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Guard, catalog checks, denial tests, fallback helper | 0 moved | — | M1 started | 2 days |
| 1 | Secrets, credentials, abuse controls | 31 | `workspace_secrets` (63 files), calendar tokens, SePay, API keys | — | 4 days |
| 2 | Billing, credits, finance | 41 | `apps/finance` on user client; `wallet_transactions` | `wallet_transactions` (M1) | 7 days |
| 3 | Mail, notifications, inquiries | 12 | `post_email_queue`, `notifications` publication | — | 3 days |
| 4 | People and identity PII | 29 | `users` (68 files), `user_private_details` (51), `workspace_users` (77) | `user_private_details` (M1) | 9 days |
| 5 | AI, meetings, memory content | 50 | AI chat, Meet AI, Mira; 15 `no-ts-caller` legacy tables | — | 4 days |
| 6 | Tasks, time, calendar content | 77 | `tasks` (81 files), browser modules in `apps/tasks`, Discord | — | 11 days |
| 7 | Education, external projects, public catalogs | 59 | Public reads (changelog, short links, Meet Together, polls) need cached server endpoints | — | 7 days |
| 8 | Workspace core and RBAC | 21 | `workspaces` (193 files), `workspace_members`, roles; RLS and storage helpers | 4 tables (M1) | 12 days |
| 9 | Function and view sweep | remaining public functions | 246 RPC names called from TS | — | 5 days |

Total: about 64 agent-days serial; about 40 with Waves 5–7 parallel. Add
production approval latency per batch and one mobile store cycle (M1) that runs
during Waves 0–1.

### Wave 0: guard and foundations

- Land the [guard](#guard-no-new-public-relations) with the full current
  allowlist (no table moves).
- Run the read-only hosted catalog check (default ACLs in `public`, RLS-off
  tables, and client grants on them) on staging, then production. Add a
  default-privilege migration only if the hosted result shows client grants
  the guard cannot exempt. It loops over the same owner roles as
  `20260522172925`, snapshots `pg_default_acl` before and after, and needs
  approval.
- Add the pgTAP denial test, the HTTP denial check and the private-first
  fallback helper in `@tuturuuu/supabase` (with tests).
- Start mobile M1: endpoints for the 6 mobile tables, Flutter repository
  switch, minimum-version plan.
- Security review of the guard and any default-privilege migration.

## Approvals and review

- **Security review (Selene)** for: the guard spec and Wave 0 migration; each
  wave's Phase B and C migrations, rollback migration and helper-schema
  changes; any allowlist addition. Review uses the exact migration SHA.
- **User approval (D138)** for every production database change. Batch to
  limit dialogs: Wave 0 default privileges (only if needed); then one dialog per batch of
  "Phase C of wave N + Phase B of wave N+1". Each dialog states the tables,
  the exact SHA, the staging marker, the rollback migration and the evidence
  (pgTAP, HTTP denial, exact-commit CI).
- Batch migration merges per wave: one combined disposable rehearsal,
  back-to-back merges, one staging marker, one production sync.
- Production evidence: the `supabase-production.yaml` exact-SHA result, a
  post-apply catalog check (tables in `private`, no client privileges), and a
  watch of 4xx/5xx rates on the affected routes. A skipped or failed workflow
  is a blocker.

## Guard: no new public relations

Two layers share the allowlist `apps/database/public-schema-allowlist.json`:

| Layer | Runs | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog: `apps/database/scripts/verify-public-schema-catalog.mjs` | `.github/workflows/public-schema-guard.yaml` on the reset CI database (full tracked migration chain in an isolated stack) | Authoritative |
| Static: `scripts/check-public-schema-objects.js` (`bun db:public-guard`) | `bun check:changed`, `bun check`, and the same workflow before the replay | Early signal, plus the shrink-only and caller rules |

### Allowlist

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "currentWave": 0,
  "lintAfterVersion": "20261117063000",
  "relations": {
    "workspaces": { "kind": "table", "wave": 8 }
  },
  "typesAhead": {
    "task_sprint_reports": {
      "wave": 6,
      "owner": "tasks board sprints",
      "reason": "Typed ahead of its migration",
      "evidence": "Absent from the replay and the production readback"
    }
  },
  "moved": {},
  "serviceRoleCompatViews": {},
  "defaultAclExemptOwners": {
    "supabase_admin": { "reason": "Platform-owned default ACL in public" }
  },
  "functions": { "enforced": false, "names": {} }
}
```

- `relations` holds every application table and view in `public` (320), each
  tagged with its wave.
- `typesAhead` records relations the generated types declare ahead of their
  migration, each with an owner, wave, reason and hosted evidence. The types
  check accepts them; the catalog check fails if one appears in `public`, so
  the migration that creates it must use `private`. An entry can only narrow
  an allowlisted relation, and it becomes stale once the types drop it.
- Moving a relation removes it from `relations` and records it in `moved`
  (`{ "wave": n, "schema": "private" }`). Moved records are permanent.
- `serviceRoleCompatViews` entries carry `expiresAfterWave` and
  `target: "private.<name>"`.
- `defaultAclExemptOwners` lists default-ACL owners the migration role cannot
  alter, each with a reason; their client grants are reported as warnings.
  `platformObjects` and `clientViewExceptions` are shrink-only; the change
  that introduces either field may populate it.
- The allowlist path is listed in `CODEOWNERS` for database and security
  owners.

### Catalog checks (authoritative)

One read-only statement reads `pg_class`, `pg_depend` and `pg_default_acl`
(extension-owned relations excluded) and fails on:

1. **G1, equality.** Every application table and view in `public` is in
   `relations` with the matching kind, and every entry exists. No
   `typesAhead` name exists in `public`. Every `moved` name exists in
   `private` and not in `public`.
2. **G2, exposure.** Every `public` table has RLS enabled. No RLS-off table
   grants `anon`, `authenticated` or `PUBLIC`. No `public` or global default
   ACL grants those roles on tables or sequences, or function EXECUTE to
   `anon` or `PUBLIC`. Default EXECUTE for `authenticated` is a warning until
   `functions.enforced` is true, then an error. Exempt owners warn.
3. **F1, platform owners.** Any `public` relation or function owned by a
   `defaultAclExemptOwners` role is an error unless recorded in
   `platformObjects` (`relation:<name>` or `function:<name>(<args>)`, each with
   a reason). Stale records fail.
4. **F2, client views.** A `public` view granted to a client role must have
   `security_invoker=true` or a reasoned `clientViewExceptions` entry. Stale
   entries fail.
5. **G5, compat views.** Each `serviceRoleCompatViews` entry exists as a plain
   view, grants no client role, reads only its `target`, and has not expired
   (`expiresAfterWave` ≥ `currentWave`).

The workflow uploads the catalog JSON as an artifact for review.

### Static checks

1. **Shrink-only (G3 fail closed).** The allowlist is compared with the one at
   the base: `PUBLIC_SCHEMA_BASE_SHA` (CI pushes pass the previous main SHA),
   else the pull request base, else the merge-base with `origin/main`. Adding
   a relation, function or exempt owner fails; removing a relation without a
   `moved` record fails; `currentWave` cannot decrease; `lintAfterVersion`
   cannot move later; function enforcement cannot be turned off. An unreadable
   base or base allowlist exits 2. The only exception is the introducing
   change, whose base has neither the allowlist nor the guard script.
2. **Generated types.** Every `public` table and view in
   `packages/types/src/supabase.ts` is allowlisted with the matching kind.
   Absence from the types is not treated as staleness: committed types can
   lag the chain, so the catalog owns that direction.
3. **Migration lint** over migrations after `lintAfterVersion`, comments
   removed. It fails on a `public` (qualified, quoted or unqualified) target
   that is not allowlisted for `CREATE [UNLOGGED] TABLE` (including
   `PARTITION OF` and `AS`), `CREATE [MATERIALIZED|RECURSIVE] VIEW`,
   `CREATE FOREIGN TABLE`, `SELECT … INTO`, `SET SCHEMA public` and
   `RENAME TO`; on literal client-role `GRANT`s on `public` relations or
   `ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public`; and on client default privileges in `public`.
   Text inside dollar-quoted bodies is scanned for creation (`EXECUTE 'create
   table …'`). Temporary relations, `search_path`-qualified private targets
   and dynamic `%I` targets are left to the catalog check. New public
   functions warn until `functions.enforced`.
4. **Direct client access** to `moved` relations: any browser-module
   reference, any Dart `.from()` in `apps/mobile/lib`, any Python `.table()` in
   `apps/discord` without `schema("private")`, and any TypeScript `.from()` not
   immediately chained from `.schema('private')`.

Exit codes for both layers: 0 pass, 1 violation, 2 setup or parse error.

### Tests

`scripts/check-public-schema-objects.test.js` covers each statement kind,
quoting, comments, dollar-quoted bodies, temporary relations, `search_path`,
dynamic targets, grants and default privileges, function warnings, every
shrink rule, compat-view expiry, the caller rules, and fail-closed base
resolution in a temporary repository.
`apps/database/scripts/public-schema-catalog.test.mjs` covers G1, G2 and G5
on catalog fixtures and fail-closed output parsing.

### Replay findings

The first full replay matched the allowlist except for three findings, all
resolved in the allowlist:

- `workspace_external_project_page_versions` is created in `public` by
  `20261109010100` and is missing from the committed types.
- `task_sprint_reports` is declared in the types and has no migration. The
  production readback confirms it is absent there too, so it is recorded
  under `typesAhead`.
- `supabase_admin` default ACLs in `public` grant `anon` and
  `authenticated` on tables, sequences and functions; the owner is exempt
  pending the hosted catalog result.

Every replayed `public` table has RLS enabled. In the replay all 320 `public`
relations and 650 functions are owned by `postgres`, and all 26 client-granted
views use `security_invoker`, so `platformObjects` and `clientViewExceptions`
start empty. 254 `public` relations (228 tables and 26 views) still grant
client roles behind RLS or `security_invoker`; the waves remove those grants.

The production readback (2026-11-17) matches: 320 relations (293 tables and
27 views), all owned by `postgres`, no RLS-off tables, and the same client
grants relation for relation as the replay.
